intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers breathtaking views of the Central Otago landscape before you freefall for 8.5 seconds. Includes transport from Queenstown and a commemorative video.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most spectacular Great Walks, traversing alpine meadows, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland National Parks. The 32km trail offers stunning views of Lake Mackenzie and Harris Saddle. Book a guided day section or multi-day hut pass.

experiences.name: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk
experiences.description: Explore the terminal face of the famous Franz Josef Glacier on a self-guided valley floor walk through ancient rainforest and glacial moraine. The trail winds through a UNESCO World Heritage landscape where ice meets temperate rainforest, a combination found almost nowhere else on Earth. Upgrade to a guided ice hike for an additional fee.

experiences.name: Queenstown Ledge Bungy
experiences.description: Jump from the original 1988 AJ Hackett bungy site perched 43 meters above the Kawarau River gorge. This historic jump is the world's first commercial bungy site and offers a thrilling yet accessible introduction to the sport, with the option to touch the water below. Includes a certificate and viewing platform for spectators.

experiences.name: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Lake
experiences.description: Walk one of New Zealand's most rewarding and accessible alpine hikes through Aoraki Mount Cook National Park. The 10km return trail crosses three swing bridges over glacial streams and leads to a stunning glacier lake with floating icebergs and jaw-dropping views of Aoraki Mount Cook, New Zealand's highest peak at 3,724 meters.
experiences.location: Aoraki Mount Cook Village, Mackenzie District

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 - no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Christchurch Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and take the budget-friendly Metro bus (Route 29, ~NZD 3.50) into the city centre. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up. Take a relaxed stroll along the Christchurch Botanic Gardens (free entry) to shake off travel fatigue and get oriented in the South Island.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Christchurch Night Market at New Regent Street or the weekly night market (seasonal). Walk around the colourful street art of the CBD Rebuild precinct. Head back to the resort for an early rest to recover from the flight.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the Christchurch Airport food court or a nearby bakery (~NZD 8–12)
meals.dinner: Dine at Lotus Heart vegetarian café or a cheap eat on Colombo Street (~NZD 12–18). Alternatively, grab groceries from a Countdown supermarket for a self-catered dinner to save money.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light due to the afternoon arrival. Pick up a South Island map and free DOC brochures from the i-SITE Visitor Centre in Christchurch. Purchase a local SIM card (Skinny or 2degrees, ~NZD 20) for maps and communication. Stock up on snacks and supplies at the supermarket tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Christchurch's free Botanic Gardens early morning for a peaceful walk among rose gardens and native bush. Walk across the Antigua Boatsheds area and along the Avon River Precinct (free). Explore the free Canterbury Museum nearby, which has excellent Maori and Antarctic exhibits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Port Hills for a hike on the free Crater Rim Walkway or the Gondola Summit Track. Take the Heathcote Valley trail up to the Summit Cross for panoramic views over Christchurch and Lyttelton Harbour. This is a moderate 2–3 hour hike with no entry fee.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city. Visit the Re:START Mall container precinct and the Cardboard Cathedral (free to view exterior). Enjoy the evening atmosphere around Oxford Terrace.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation using supermarket supplies (~NZD 5–8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the supermarket enjoyed on the Port Hills (~NZD 6–10)
meals.dinner: Try Burger Fuel or Hell Pizza for a budget-friendly NZ meal (~NZD 14–18), or cook at the hostel kitchen

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the Port Hills hike. Sunscreen is essential as NZ UV levels are very high in November. Check the DOC website for any track closures before heading out.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the scenic drive south toward Lake Tekapo (~3 hours from Christchurch). Stop at Rakaia Gorge lookout en route for free views of the turquoise glacial river. Arrive at Lake Tekapo by mid-morning and walk to the iconic Church of the Good Shepherd (free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Mount John Summit Loop Track (~2 hours, free), which offers spectacular 360-degree views over the turquoise Lake Tekapo and the Mackenzie Basin. This is a rewarding moderate hike with no entry fee. Alternatively, take the shorter Tekapo B Power Station Walk along the canal.
day_by_day.evening: Lake Tekapo is one of the world's best stargazing spots (Dark Sky Reserve). Visit the Tekapo Springs lakefront area at dusk. Consider the budget-friendly self-guided stargazing from the lakefront (free) rather than the paid observatory tour.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before departing Christchurch (~NZD 5–8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Lake Tekapo lakefront (~NZD 6–10)
meals.dinner: Cook at the accommodation kitchen or try Mackenzie's Bar & Grill for a budget meal (~NZD 16–22)

day_by_day.notes: Budget accommodation options in Lake Tekapo include YHA Lake Tekapo or Tailor-Made Tekapo Hostel (~NZD 30–45/night dorm). Book ahead as Tekapo gets busy in summer. Bring warm layers — evenings can be cold even in November.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Lake Tekapo to Aoraki / Mount Cook (~1.5 hours). Stop at Lake Pukaki lookout for the iconic turquoise glacier-fed lake with Mount Cook in the background — one of NZ's most photographed views (free). Arrive at Mount Cook Village and check in to YHA Aoraki Mount Cook (~NZD 35–50/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the famous Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Lake — one of New Zealand's most rewarding and accessible alpine hikes. The 10km return trail winds through Aoraki Mount Cook National Park past swing bridges, glacial lakes, and dramatic mountain scenery. Mueller Lake at the end offers stunning views of Mount Cook. Allow 3–4 hours return. Free DOC track.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village. Visit the Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre (small entry fee ~NZD 5) for a planetarium show and mountaineering history. Enjoy the sunset alpenglow on Aoraki Mount Cook from the village lookout.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Lake Tekapo accommodation before departure (~NZD 5–8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Hooker Valley Track at Mueller Lake (~NZD 6–10)
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at YHA kitchen or grab a budget meal at the Old Mountaineers Café (~NZD 18–25)

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is suitable for all fitness levels but wear proper footwear. Weather can change rapidly — bring a rain jacket and extra layers. The track can be busy in the afternoon; starting before 2pm is recommended. This is a highlight of the entire trip.

day_by_day.morning: Wake early for sunrise views of Aoraki Mount Cook from the Kea Point Track (2km return, 1 hour, free). This short walk gives dramatic views of the Mueller Glacier and Mount Cook face. Alternatively, start the Red Tarns Track for elevated views over the valley (~1.5 hours return).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive west toward the West Coast via the Haast Pass Highway. Stop at the Blue Pools Walk near Makarora (~30 min return walk, free) to see crystal-clear blue glacial pools. Continue driving through the stunning Haast Pass and Gates of Haast gorge. Arrive in Fox Glacier township (~3.5 hours total drive).
day_by_day.evening: Check in to budget accommodation in Fox Glacier (Ivory Towers Lodge or Fox Glacier Holiday Park, ~NZD 30–45). Explore the small township and grab dinner. Check weather forecast for Franz Josef Glacier visit tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at YHA Mount Cook (~NZD 5–8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Blue Pools or eaten in the car during the scenic drive (~NZD 6–10)
meals.dinner: Cook at the hostel kitchen or try the Fox Glacier Tavern for a budget pub meal (~NZD 16–22)

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Mount Cook to Fox Glacier via Haast Pass is one of NZ's most scenic routes — allow extra time for photo stops. Fill up on petrol before leaving Mount Cook as fuel stations are scarce on the West Coast. The Haast Pass road can be affected by weather — check NZ Transport Agency road conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 25 minutes north to Franz Josef Glacier. Complete the Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk — a self-guided valley floor walk to the terminal face of the famous Franz Josef Glacier. The walk is free, takes approximately 1.5–2 hours return, and offers dramatic views of the glacier descending from the Southern Alps. Follow DOC safety signs carefully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Fox Glacier and hike the Fox Glacier Valley Walk (similar free self-guided walk to Fox Glacier terminal face, ~1.5 hours return). This gives you a comparison of two of NZ's most famous glaciers in one day. Alternatively, hike the Lake Matheson Walk (~1.5 hours, free) for the iconic 'Mirror Lake' reflection of Mount Cook and Mount Tasman.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the accommodation. If budget allows, consider the Glacier Hot Pools in Franz Josef (~NZD 29) for a well-earned soak. Otherwise, enjoy the West Coast rainforest atmosphere and star gaze from the township.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Fox Glacier accommodation (~NZD 5–8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Franz Josef or grab a cheap bite at a local café (~NZD 8–12)
meals.dinner: Cook at the hostel kitchen or try Alice May restaurant in Franz Josef for a budget meal (~NZD 16–22)

day_by_day.notes: The glacier valley walks are free but guided glacier hikes are available for ~NZD 149+ if budget allows. Always stay behind DOC safety barriers at the glacier terminal face — ice and rock falls are a genuine hazard. Lake Matheson is best visited at dawn or dusk for the clearest reflections.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Fox Glacier toward Wanaka (~3.5 hours via Haast). Stop at Knights Point Lookout for free coastal views over the Tasman Sea. Pass through the tiny settlement of Haast and stop at the Haast Visitor Centre (free DOC information centre with excellent rainforest and ecology displays).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Wanaka by early afternoon. Check in to budget accommodation (Wanaka Bakpaka or Base Wanaka, ~NZD 30–45/night). Take a walk along the Wanaka lakefront (free) and visit the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' — the lone willow tree in Lake Wanaka. Hike the short Mount Iron Track (~1.5 hours return, free) for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the lakefront at sunset. Explore Wanaka's small but vibrant town centre. Visit the free Puzzling World exterior or browse the local shops.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Fox Glacier before departure (~NZD 5–8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the road or at Haast (~NZD 6–10)
meals.dinner: Try Kai Whakapai Café & Bar on the lakefront or grab a cheap pizza from Francesca's Italian Kitchen (~NZD 14–20)

day_by_day.notes: Wanaka is a great base for the next few days. Stock up at the New World supermarket for self-catering supplies. The town is smaller and slightly less touristy than Queenstown, making it a great budget-friendly alternative. Book Queenstown bungee jumping in advance online for best prices.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Rob Roy Glacier Track from the Matukituki Valley (~4 hours return, free DOC track). This is one of Wanaka's best hikes, offering views of a hanging glacier, waterfalls, and alpine meadows. Drive ~55 minutes from Wanaka to the Raspberry Creek car park (4WD recommended but standard cars can manage in dry conditions).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Rob Roy hike or, if returning early, explore the Diamond Lake & Rocky Mountain Track near Wanaka (~2 hours return, free) for more great views over Lake Wanaka and the Matukituki Valley.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Wanaka for a well-earned rest. Visit the Wanaka lakefront for sunset. Grab dinner and plan the Queenstown bungee adventure for the coming days.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before the drive to Matukituki (~NZD 5–8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at the Rob Roy Glacier viewpoint (~NZD 6–10)
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the hostel kitchen or try Burrito Bar Wanaka for a budget-friendly meal (~NZD 12–16)

day_by_day.notes: The Rob Roy Glacier Track requires a river crossing that can be impassable after heavy rain — check conditions with DOC before going. Start early to avoid afternoon crowds. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and a rain jacket. This is one of the best free hikes in the South Island.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Wanaka to Queenstown (~1 hour via Crown Range Road — the highest sealed road in NZ with spectacular views, free). Stop at the Crown Range Summit viewpoint. Arrive in Queenstown and check in to budget accommodation (Nomads Queenstown or Base Queenstown, ~NZD 35–55/night dorm).
day_by_day.afternoon: BUNGEE JUMPING EXPERIENCE: Head to the AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungy (~NZD 165–185) — the world's first commercial bungee jump site, 43 metres above the Kawarau River. This is the most iconic and budget-friendly of Queenstown's bungee options. Watching jumpers from the viewing platform is free if you want to observe first.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungee jump! Explore Queenstown's vibrant waterfront and Steamer Wharf area. Walk along the lakefront and enjoy views of the Remarkables mountain range at sunset. Browse the lively Queenstown Mall area.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Wanaka before departure (~NZD 5–8)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Queenstown's Ferg Burger (famous NZ institution, ~NZD 14–18) — worth the splurge
meals.dinner: Cook at the hostel kitchen to save money after the bungee spend, or try the Queenstown Night Market (Thursday–Sunday, ~NZD 10–15)

day_by_day.notes: Book Kawarau Bridge Bungy online in advance for the best price and to secure your preferred time slot. The jump is filmed and photographed — packages are available but optional. Minimum weight is 35kg, maximum 180kg. Arrive 30 minutes before your jump time. The adrenaline rush will be unforgettable!

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Ben Lomond Track from Queenstown (free DOC track). Take the Queenstown Gondola up (~NZD 39 return, optional — you can hike up for free) then continue to the Ben Lomond summit (~1748m, 4–5 hours return from gondola). Offers 360-degree views over Queenstown, Lake Wakatipu, and the Remarkables.
day_by_day.afternoon: If energy allows, continue the Ben Lomond hike. Alternatively, descend and explore the Queenstown Gardens (free) — a peaceful peninsula park with rose gardens, disc golf, and lakefront walks. Visit the free Kiwi Birdlife Park entrance area or just enjoy the lakefront.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Queenstown waterfront at sunset. Explore the lively Shotover Street restaurant and bar strip. Enjoy the electric atmosphere of Queenstown at night.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hostel (~NZD 5–8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Ben Lomond summit or Queenstown Gardens (~NZD 6–10)
meals.dinner: Try Vudu Café & Larder for a budget dinner, or grab fish and chips from a local takeaway (~NZD 12–16)

day_by_day.notes: The Ben Lomond Track is challenging — only attempt the summit if you are fit and the weather is clear. The track can be icy or wet — check DOC conditions. Alternatively, the Tiki Trail hike up to the gondola summit is free and offers great views with less effort (~2 hours return). Queenstown can be expensive — stick to self-catering where possible.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the stunning Glenorchy Road from Queenstown to Glenorchy (~45 minutes, free). Stop at multiple viewpoints along Lake Wakatipu — one of NZ's most scenic drives. Arrive in the tiny village of Glenorchy and hike the Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway (~1 hour return, free) through wetlands with mountain reflections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike part of the Routeburn Track from the Glenorchy end (free DOC track). The first section to Routeburn Flats (~4 hours return) is accessible as a day walk and offers stunning beech forest and mountain scenery without requiring a multi-day booking. This is a world-famous Great Walk.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Queenstown along the lake. Enjoy the golden hour light on Lake Wakatipu. Grab dinner and pack bags for the drive toward Te Anau tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the Queenstown hostel (~NZD 5–8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Routeburn Track (~NZD 6–10)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the hostel or try a cheap meal at Queenstown's Countdown supermarket deli (~NZD 10–15)

day_by_day.notes: The Glenorchy area was used as a filming location for Lord of the Rings — fans will recognise several landscapes. The full Routeburn Track is a 3-day Great Walk requiring hut bookings, but the day walk section is free and spectacular. Bring insect repellent as sandflies can be fierce near Glenorchy.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Te Anau (~2 hours). Stop at Kingston and the Kingston Flyer historic railway site. Arrive in Te Anau — the gateway to Fiordland National Park. Check in to budget accommodation (YHA Te Anau or Te Anau Top 10 Holiday Park, ~NZD 30–45/night). Visit the free DOC Fiordland National Park Visitor Centre for excellent displays on the park's ecology.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Kepler Track Day Walk — take the free DOC track from the Te Anau lakefront to the Kepler Track control gates and hike through ancient beech forest to the Brod Bay picnic area (~2–3 hours return). Alternatively, hike the Mount Luxmore lower slopes for panoramic views (~3 hours return, free).
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Te Anau lakefront at sunset. Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves boat tour (~NZD 55) if budget allows — a unique underground cave experience. Otherwise, enjoy the peaceful lakeside atmosphere for free.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Queenstown before departure (~NZD 5–8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Kepler Track at Brod Bay (~NZD 6–10)
meals.dinner: Try The Fat Duck restaurant for a budget meal or grab fish and chips from a local takeaway in Te Anau (~NZD 14–20)

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau is the last major town before Milford Sound — stock up on groceries and fuel here. The Te Anau Glowworm Caves tour is genuinely magical and worth the splurge if budget allows. Book ahead as tours fill up quickly. Sandflies are very common in Fiordland — pack strong insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the spectacular drive from Te Anau to Milford Sound (~2 hours via the Milford Road — one of the world's great scenic drives). Stop at Mirror Lakes (free boardwalk), The Divide viewpoint, and the Homer Tunnel. Arrive at Milford Sound and take a budget Milford Sound cruise (~NZD 45–75 for a 2-hour nature cruise) to see Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, and wildlife including dolphins and seals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return drive from Milford Sound back toward Te Anau and then Queenstown (~4.5 hours total). Stop at Monkey Creek and Lake Gunn Nature Walk (~45 min loop, free) through ancient podocarp forest on the return journey. Arrive back in Queenstown by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Queenstown. Celebrate the end of an amazing South Island adventure with a meal out at Ferg Burger or the Queenstown Night Market. Take a final walk along the lakefront and reflect on 13 incredible days of hiking, bungee jumping, and exploring.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered very early breakfast at Te Anau before the Milford drive (~NZD 5–8)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Milford Sound before or after the cruise (~NZD 6–10)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a final celebratory dinner at Ferg Burger or a Queenstown restaurant (~NZD 16–25)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Milford Sound cruise well in advance — it is one of NZ's most popular attractions and prices are lower when booked online ahead of time. Real Journeys and Go Orange offer competitive budget prices. The Milford Road can close due to avalanche risk in bad weather — check NZ Transport Agency road conditions the night before. This is the perfect finale to an epic South Island adventure!

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Christchurch or Queenstown airport, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get oriented. Explore the immediate resort surroundings and enjoy the coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed welcome dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby casual eatery. Review the 13-day itinerary, confirm activity bookings, and get an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light bite at the airport or a café near the resort after check-in — try a classic NZ meat pie or sandwich (~NZD 10–15)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's on-site restaurant or a nearby mid-range spot — look for fresh local seafood or a hearty NZ lamb dish (~NZD 30–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Nothing is scheduled before 13:00. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm all pre-booked experiences (Nevis Bungy, Routeburn Track, etc.) and check weather forecasts for the coming days. Purchase a local SIM card at the airport if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the local area around the resort on foot. If based near Queenstown, walk the Queenstown Bay Promenade along Lake Wakatipu — a flat, scenic 3–4 km lakeside walk with stunning Remarkables mountain views. Great way to ease into the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Queenstown Gardens — a peaceful peninsula park with rose gardens, a frisbee golf course, and lake views. Rent a bike from a local hire shop and cycle the dedicated Queenstown Trail sections near town (~NZD 35–50 for half-day hire).
day_by_day.evening: Head into Queenstown town centre. Browse the lively waterfront and enjoy the buzzing atmosphere of New Zealand's adventure capital.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort or a local café — try a classic Kiwi 'big breakfast' with eggs, bacon, and toast (~NZD 18–25)
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a lakeside café — try a fresh salad bowl or fish tacos (~NZD 18–28)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range Queenstown restaurant such as Rata or a local bistro — try NZ venison or salmon (~NZD 35–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is an acclimatisation day. Use it to get comfortable with the area, check gear, and confirm upcoming adventure bookings. November is late spring in NZ — expect mild to warm weather with occasional showers.

day_by_day.morning: QUEENSTOWN LEDGE BUNGY — Head to the iconic Kawarau Bridge (original 1988 AJ Hackett site), 43 meters above the Kawarau River gorge. This is the world's first commercial bungy site and a legendary experience. Book the first session of the day (~NZD 175–205 per person). Spectators can watch for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, recover with a scenic drive or e-bike ride through the Gibbston Valley wine region, just 15 minutes from Kawarau Bridge. Visit a local cellar door for a wine tasting — Gibbston Valley Winery or Chard Farm offer excellent Pinot Noir (~NZD 10–20 tasting fee).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for a celebratory dinner. Relive the bungy jump experience and share photos.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before heading out — cereal, toast, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Gibbston Valley Winery restaurant or a picnic from a local deli — cheese, charcuterie, and local wine (~NZD 25–40)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Queenstown restaurant — try Botswana Butchery or a mid-range steakhouse for a celebratory meal (~NZD 40–60 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kawarau Ledge Bungy well in advance through AJ Hackett's website. Wear comfortable, close-fitting clothes. Avoid a heavy meal immediately before jumping. Weight limits apply (45–118 kg). GoPro footage packages are available for purchase on-site (~NZD 50–80).

day_by_day.morning: NEVIS BUNGY JUMP — Take on New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. A shuttle from Queenstown takes you to the remote site (~NZD 275–320 per person, including transfer). The pod is suspended by cables above the canyon — an unforgettable freefall experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Nevis experience, return to Queenstown by shuttle (included). Spend the afternoon relaxing — visit the Queenstown Hill Time Walk, a 2-hour loop trail above town offering panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables. Easy to moderate grade.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening at the resort to rest muscles and prepare gear for the upcoming Routeburn Track multi-day hike.

meals.breakfast: Substantial breakfast before departure — eggs, protein, and coffee. Eat at least 2 hours before jumping
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch or grab food at the Nevis base station — energy bars, sandwiches (~NZD 15–20)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner near the resort or in town — try a burger or pizza at a local spot (~NZD 25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy requires a specific shuttle from Queenstown — do not attempt to drive yourself. Weight limits: 45–127 kg. This is the most intense bungy on the itinerary — if doing both Kawarau and Nevis, consider spacing them out more if you feel sore. Book through AJ Hackett. Prepare hiking gear for Days 5–7.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer from Queenstown to the Routeburn Track trailhead (Routeburn Shelter end, ~1.5 hours drive). Begin the ROUTEBURN TRACK GREAT WALK — Day 1 of 3. Hike from Routeburn Shelter to Routeburn Flats Hut (~2 hours, 6.7 km, easy grade). Pass through ancient beech forest along the Routeburn River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Routeburn Flats to Routeburn Falls Hut (~1.5 hours, 2.3 km, moderate-steep). Gain significant elevation with spectacular waterfall views. Arrive at Routeburn Falls Hut (1,000m elevation) and settle in.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Routeburn Falls Hut with views over the Hollyford Valley. Meet fellow trampers, cook dinner using hut facilities, and stargaze from one of the most dramatic hut locations in New Zealand.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or a packed meal before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — wraps, nuts, dried fruit, energy bars (prepare the night before)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal at the hut using gas cookers — dehydrated meals or pre-packed ingredients (~NZD 10–15 per meal)

day_by_day.notes: Great Walks hut passes MUST be booked in advance through DOC (Department of Conservation) — book months ahead as they sell out fast (~NZD 70–80 per night per person). Carry all food for 3 days. Pack rain gear — weather in Fiordland/Mt Aspiring area is highly changeable. November is shoulder season with longer daylight hours.

day_by_day.morning: ROUTEBURN TRACK — Day 2. Hike from Routeburn Falls Hut over the Harris Saddle (1,255m) — the highest point of the track. On a clear day, views stretch across Fiordland and the Tasman Sea. (~4–5 hours to Lake Mackenzie Hut, 11.4 km, moderate-hard).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Lake Mackenzie Hut, set beside a stunning alpine lake surrounded by beech forest. Arrive early afternoon — take a refreshing swim in the lake if weather permits, or simply rest and take in the scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the golden evening light over Lake Mackenzie. Cook dinner at the hut, write in a journal, and rest well for the final day of the track.

meals.breakfast: Hot oats or muesli cooked at the hut — pack instant oats and dried fruit
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch — crackers, cheese, salami, chocolate, and energy gels
meals.dinner: Dehydrated backcountry meal at the hut — options like pasta bolognese or chicken risotto (~NZD 12–18)

day_by_day.notes: The Harris Saddle section is exposed and can be dangerous in high winds or snow — check DOC weather updates before departing. A side trip to Conical Hill from the saddle adds 1 hour but offers breathtaking 360° views. Poles are recommended for the descent. Stay on marked track at all times.

day_by_day.morning: ROUTEBURN TRACK — Day 3 (Final Day). Hike from Lake Mackenzie Hut to The Divide (southern trailhead), ~3–4 hours, 9.3 km, moderate. Pass through the Hollyford Valley, Lake Howden, and through more stunning beech forest. Reach The Divide by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Catch the pre-arranged shuttle or InterIslander bus back toward Queenstown (~2.5 hours). Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Shower, rest, and recover. Do laundry if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Celebration dinner in Queenstown after completing the Routeburn Track — a well-earned treat!

meals.breakfast: Final hut breakfast — instant coffee, oats, and remaining snacks
meals.lunch: Grab food at The Divide or on the shuttle — pack remaining trail snacks
meals.dinner: Special dinner at a quality Queenstown restaurant — try The Bunker or a lakeside restaurant for a post-track feast (~NZD 45–65 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your shuttle from The Divide back to Queenstown — Tracknet and Alpinelink offer reliable services. Confirm pickup time when booking the track. The Divide is accessible only by shuttle or private vehicle — there is no public transport. Rest your legs tonight — more adventures ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day after the Routeburn Track. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast, and take a gentle walk along the beachfront or lakeside. Visit a local spa or hot pool for muscle recovery — Onsen Hot Pools near Queenstown offers private cedar hot tubs overlooking the Arrow River (~NZD 55–75 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a local bus to Arrowtown (~25 minutes from Queenstown) — a beautifully preserved 1860s gold rush town. Explore the Chinese Settlement historic site, browse boutique shops, and walk along the Arrow River. Free to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Arrowtown before returning to the resort — the town has excellent mid-range restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — eggs benedict, fresh juice, and good coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch in Arrowtown — try The Fork and Tap pub or Provisions café (~NZD 20–30)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Saffron Restaurant in Arrowtown (mid-range, excellent local cuisine) or a casual bistro (~NZD 35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest day — your legs need recovery after 3 days of hiking. Arrowtown is a highlight of the Queenstown Lakes region and easily combined with a relaxed day. The Onsen Hot Pools must be booked in advance. November evenings are long — sunset around 9:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown toward Mount Cook (Aoraki) — approximately 3.5–4 hours via SH6 and SH8 through the Mackenzie Basin. Stop at Lake Tekapo en route — walk around the famous Church of the Good Shepherd and enjoy the impossibly blue glacial lake views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Aoraki/Mount Cook Village. Check into accommodation (pre-booked lodge or YHA). Begin the HOOKER VALLEY TRACK TO MUELLER LAKE — one of NZ's most rewarding accessible alpine hikes. 5 km return, 2–3 hours, easy-moderate grade. Cross three swing bridges with direct views of Aoraki/Mt Cook (3,724m).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village for dinner. The Mackenzie Basin is one of NZ's Dark Sky Reserves — on a clear night, the stargazing is world-class. Join a guided stargazing tour or simply lie on the grass and look up.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure — pack road trip snacks
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Lake Tekapo — pick up supplies from a Queenstown supermarket the night before, or grab food at a Tekapo café (~NZD 15–25)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Old Mountaineers' Café & Bar in Mt Cook Village — hearty meals with incredible mountain views (~NZD 30–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The drive through the Mackenzie Basin is spectacular — allow extra time for photo stops at Lake Pukaki (the most vivid turquoise colour you'll ever see). Book Mt Cook accommodation well in advance — options are limited and fill up fast. The Hooker Valley Track is well-marked and suitable for most fitness levels. Wear layers — temperatures drop quickly at altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning walk — the Kea Point Track (2 hours return, easy) offers stunning views of the Mueller Glacier and Hooker Valley from above. Start at 7:00–8:00 AM for the best light and fewest crowds. Watch for kea (alpine parrots) — curious and cheeky birds native to NZ mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Mt Cook toward the West Coast — approximately 4 hours via SH8 and SH6 through Haast Pass (one of NZ's most dramatic alpine highways). Stop at Haast Pass viewpoints and Thunder Creek Falls (a 5-minute walk to a stunning 28m waterfall).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Franz Josef Glacier township on the West Coast. Check into accommodation. The West Coast has a unique, rugged, rainforest-meets-glacier atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Mt Cook Village café or self-catered at accommodation
meals.lunch: Packed lunch for the road — eat at a scenic Haast Pass viewpoint or picnic area
meals.dinner: Dinner in Franz Josef township — try The Landing restaurant or a local pub for West Coast whitebait fritters (a regional specialty) (~NZD 25–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Haast Pass road (SH6) is one of the most scenic drives in New Zealand — allow 5+ hours with stops. Fuel up before leaving Mt Cook area as petrol stations are sparse. West Coast weather is notoriously wet — pack waterproof gear. Whitebait fritters are a must-try West Coast delicacy.

day_by_day.morning: FRANZ JOSEF GLACIER VALLEY WALK — Self-guided walk to the terminal face of the famous Franz Josef Glacier. The valley floor walk is approximately 4 km return, 1.5–2 hours, easy grade. Walk through a dramatic gorge of rock and ice melt, with signposted viewpoints progressively closer to the glacier face. Free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: For an enhanced glacier experience, consider a helicopter scenic flight over the glacier and Southern Alps — Franz Josef offers numerous operators (e.g., Glacier Helicopters, Air Safaris). A 20-minute scenic flight with a snow landing costs ~NZD 280–350 per person and is an extraordinary mid-range splurge worth considering.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Franz Josef village. Visit the West Coast Wildlife Centre to see kiwi birds in a nocturnal house (~NZD 35 per person) — a rare chance to see NZ's national bird up close.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café — try eggs on toast with a flat white coffee (~NZD 18–25)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a café in Franz Josef village after the glacier walk — soup and sandwich or a toasted panini (~NZD 18–28)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alice May restaurant in Franz Josef — popular local spot with good pasta and pizza options (~NZD 28–42 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Always stay behind the safety barriers at the glacier — the terminal face is unstable and rock/ice falls occur without warning. DOC updates the safe viewing distance regularly. The helicopter flight is optional but highly recommended if budget allows — the aerial view of the glacier is transformative. Book ahead in peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Franz Josef toward Queenstown — a long but spectacular 4.5–5 hour drive via Haast and the Haast Pass. Stop at Knights Point Lookout for dramatic Tasman Sea coastal views, and pause at Ship Creek for a short rainforest boardwalk (20 minutes, free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Wanaka — stop for 1–2 hours. Walk the Wanaka lakefront, visit the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' (a lone willow growing in the lake), and grab a coffee. Wanaka is a beautiful, quieter alternative to Queenstown.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Queenstown / Aegean Bliss Resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy a final evening in Queenstown — perhaps a sunset lake cruise or simply a walk along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Franz Josef before departure — fuel up for the long drive
meals.lunch: Lunch in Wanaka — try Francesca's Italian Kitchen or a lakeside café (~NZD 20–30)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a favourite Queenstown restaurant — revisit a highlight from earlier in the trip or try somewhere new (~NZD 35–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Haast Highway (SH6) is long and winding — take regular breaks and do not rush. Fill up with petrol in Haast as there are limited stations. Wanaka is a lovely detour — Puzzling World (~NZD 20) and Roy's Peak Track are other options if time allows. The drive from Wanaka to Queenstown through the Crown Range Road (weather permitting) is one of NZ's most scenic — adds 30 minutes but worth it.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in New Zealand. Take a slow farewell walk along the resort beachfront or lakeside — soak in the last views of the Southern Alps and Lake Wakatipu. Visit a local café for a final flat white and breakfast. Pick up souvenirs — try the Queenstown markets or local shops for NZ Manuka honey, Merino wool products, or pounamu (greenstone) jewellery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Transfer to Queenstown Airport for departure. Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Reflect on 13 incredible days of bungy jumping, glacier walks, alpine hikes, and South Island scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Farewell, New Zealand!

meals.breakfast: Final NZ breakfast at a local café — smashed avo on toast or a full Kiwi breakfast with a farewell flat white (~NZD 18–28)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a final takeaway from a Queenstown favourite
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time carefully and plan the resort checkout accordingly. Queenstown Airport is small but can get busy — arrive early. Ensure all gear (especially hiking boots and wet items) are properly packed and within luggage limits. New Zealand has strict biosecurity — declare or dispose of any food, soil, or plant material before departure. Keep a NZD 25–50 cash buffer for airport snacks or last-minute purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers breathtaking views of the Central Otago landscape before you freefall for 8.5 seconds. Includes transport from Queenstown and a commemorative video.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most spectacular Great Walks, traversing alpine meadows, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland National Parks. The 32km trail offers stunning views of Lake Mackenzie and Harris Saddle. Book a guided day section or multi-day hut pass.

experiences.name: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk
experiences.description: Explore the terminal face of the famous Franz Josef Glacier on a self-guided valley floor walk through ancient rainforest and glacial moraine. The trail winds through a UNESCO World Heritage landscape where ice meets temperate rainforest, a combination found almost nowhere else on Earth. Upgrade to a guided ice hike for an additional fee.

experiences.name: Queenstown Ledge Bungy
experiences.description: Jump from the original 1988 AJ Hackett bungy site perched 43 meters above the Kawarau River gorge. This historic jump is the world's first commercial bungy site and offers a thrilling yet accessible introduction to the sport, with the option to touch the water below. Includes a certificate and viewing platform for spectators.

experiences.name: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Lake
experiences.description: Walk one of New Zealand's most rewarding and accessible alpine hikes through Aoraki Mount Cook National Park. The 10km return trail crosses three swing bridges over glacial streams and leads to a stunning glacier lake with floating icebergs and jaw-dropping views of Aoraki Mount Cook, New Zealand's highest peak at 3,724 meters.
experiences.location: Aoraki Mount Cook Village, Mackenzie District

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands and you clear customs/immigration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in to your beachfront suite, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll along the beachfront to acclimate to the stunning South Island scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant. Enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring South Island specialties such as Marlborough salmon, Canterbury lamb, and Central Otago Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Light refreshments at the airport or en route via private transfer with a pre-arranged gourmet picnic hamper
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — 5-course tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in if possible. Keep the afternoon relaxed to recover from long-haul travel. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings with the resort concierge this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Guided sunrise coastal walk along the beachfront near the resort. Breathe in the fresh South Island air and take in panoramic ocean views. A private naturalist guide points out local flora and seabirds endemic to the region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private helicopter scenic flight over the surrounding landscape — coastline, glaciers, and alpine peaks depending on resort location. Land at a remote alpine viewpoint for a champagne toast before returning.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your private beachfront terrace followed by a premium seafood dinner at a nearby acclaimed restaurant, featuring Bluff oysters, green-lipped mussels, and crayfish.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh fruit platters, artisan pastries, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Champagne and charcuterie picnic at the alpine helicopter landing point
meals.dinner: Local acclaimed seafood restaurant — à la carte with sommelier-selected New Zealand white wines

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter scenic flight is weather-dependent — confirm the morning of. Book 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Dress in layers for the helicopter excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding session along the beachfront coastline with a certified instructor. Explore sea caves and hidden coves inaccessible by road.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a full afternoon at the resort's luxury spa — signature South Island stone massage, body wrap using locally sourced manuka honey and sea kelp, and a private hydrotherapy session.
day_by_day.evening: Private chef's table experience at the resort — watch the executive chef prepare a bespoke 7-course degustation menu using hyper-local ingredients, paired with rare Central Otago and Marlborough wines.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast delivered to your beachfront suite — smashed avocado on sourdough, poached eggs, fresh-pressed juices, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light spa lunch — raw salads, cold-pressed juices, and protein bowls served poolside
meals.dinner: Chef's table degustation — 7 courses with matched wine pairing, including a rare aged Pinot Noir from Central Otago

day_by_day.notes: Book the chef's table experience at least 3 days in advance as it is limited to 8 guests. Spa treatments should also be pre-booked. Check kayak/SUP availability with the resort's activities desk.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Queenstown (approximately 3–4 hours depending on resort location, or 45-minute scenic charter flight). Check in to a luxury Queenstown property or day-use suite. Morning arrival — enjoy a lakeside espresso at a premium Queenstown café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Queenstown Ledge Bungy — Jump from the original 1988 AJ Hackett bungy site, 43 meters above the Kawarau River gorge. This iconic leap is a bucket-list experience with stunning gorge views. A VIP package includes private viewing platform, video/photo package, and a post-jump certificate.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungy milestone with dinner at Queenstown's finest restaurant — Rata by Josh Emett or equivalent, featuring New Zealand premium produce with a contemporary fine-dining approach. Reserve a window table overlooking the lake.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — continental spread with fresh local produce
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at a lakefront Queenstown restaurant — venison burger, truffle fries, and craft beer or local wine
meals.dinner: Rata by Josh Emett or equivalent fine-dining Queenstown restaurant — seasonal tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book Kawarau Bungy VIP package through AJ Hackett at least 1 week in advance. Wear comfortable, close-toed shoes. Weight restrictions apply — check requirements. Charter flight option from resort adds approximately 45 minutes of spectacular scenic views.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. A private 4WD transfers you to the Nevis site. The VIP experience includes a dedicated host, private gondola cabin, unlimited jumps option, and a full media package with drone footage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Recovery and adrenaline celebration — private wine tasting at a Central Otago vineyard (Amisfield, Peregrine, or Felton Road). Be chauffeured through stunning schist rock and alpine landscape to taste world-class Pinot Noir and Riesling at cellar door.
day_by_day.evening: Lakeside dinner at a premium Queenstown restaurant with views over Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables mountain range. Enjoy a celebratory bottle of Central Otago Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: High-protein breakfast before the jump — eggs, smoked salmon, avocado, and strong coffee at a Queenstown café
meals.lunch: Vineyard platter lunch at the cellar door — artisan cheeses, cured meats, fresh bread, and estate wines
meals.dinner: Lakeside fine-dining restaurant — Canterbury lamb rack, truffle risotto, and a sommelier-curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy requires advance booking — secure VIP package directly with AJ Hackett. Minimum age 10, no upper age limit but medical conditions must be disclosed. Vineyard visits should be booked in advance. Do not eat a heavy meal before the jump.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic Milford Sound day trip — private charter or small-group luxury cruise. Depart Queenstown early by private coach or scenic flight to Milford Sound. Witness dramatic fiords, Mitre Peak, and cascading waterfalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury Milford Sound cruise aboard a premium vessel — kayaking in the fiord, wildlife spotting (dolphins, seals, penguins), and an underwater observatory visit. Champagne and gourmet canapés served on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown by scenic flight (recommended) for golden-hour aerial views of Fiordland. Quiet dinner at the hotel or a local bistro — relaxed evening after a full day of exploration.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast from the hotel — thermos coffee, fresh muffins, fruit, and yogurt for the road
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch served aboard the luxury Milford Sound cruise — smoked salmon, New Zealand cheeses, and Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc
meals.dinner: Casual fine-dining bistro in Queenstown — pan-seared blue cod, seasonal vegetables, and Central Otago Pinot Gris

day_by_day.notes: Milford Sound is approximately 4 hours by road from Queenstown. A scenic flight one-way (either to or from) is highly recommended and adds significant value. Book well in advance — Milford Sound is one of New Zealand's most popular destinations. Weather can be unpredictable; rain actually enhances the waterfalls.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Great Walk — Day 1 of a 2-day private guided hike. Depart Queenstown by private transfer to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead. Begin the iconic alpine traverse through ancient beech forest, crossing crystal-clear streams and ascending toward the alpine zone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking to Routeburn Falls Hut area — the private guided experience includes a dedicated gourmet guide who carries a premium picnic. Reach Routeburn Falls for spectacular views of the Falls Cirque and surrounding peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at Routeburn Falls Lodge (private lodge booking for exclusive use or premium bunk). Enjoy a hot, chef-prepared dinner in the hut, stargazing in pristine dark skies, and a debrief with your guide on tomorrow's alpine section.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at Queenstown accommodation before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail picnic prepared by your guide — antipasto, artisan sandwiches, energy bars, and thermos of soup
meals.dinner: Hot chef-prepared dinner at Routeburn Falls Lodge — hearty mountain cuisine with wine

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track requires advance booking through the Department of Conservation (DOC) for hut passes — book months in advance as it is one of New Zealand's Great Walks. A private guided experience with Ultimate Hikes or similar operator provides gourmet meals and dedicated guiding. Pack layers, waterproof jacket, and broken-in hiking boots.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Great Walk — Day 2. Rise early for sunrise views from the alpine zone. Continue the traverse over Harris Saddle (1,255m) — the highest point of the track — with panoramic views across Fiordland and the Darran Mountains on a clear day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through the Hollyford Valley side, passing Lake Mackenzie and the stunning beech forest canopy. Private transfer meets you at the Divide or Routeburn Shelter to return to Queenstown. Freshen up at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Celebration dinner at Queenstown's top restaurant — a full degustation experience to reward two days of world-class hiking. Pair with an exceptional Central Otago Pinot Noir from a small-batch producer.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge, eggs, and coffee at Routeburn Falls Lodge before the day's hike
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail picnic at Lake Mackenzie — smoked meats, cheese, crackers, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Top-tier Queenstown fine-dining restaurant — 8-course degustation with premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Harris Saddle can be exposed to wind and weather — your guide will assess conditions. The full Routeburn traverse is approximately 32km over 2 days. Ensure hiking boots are well broken-in before this trip. Private transfer from the Divide back to Queenstown takes approximately 1.5 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in and enjoy a luxurious in-room breakfast. Optional: gentle yoga session with a private instructor arranged by the hotel, or a soak in the hotel's heated pool with Remarkables views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Franz Josef (approximately 4–5 hours scenic drive through Haast Pass, or 1-hour scenic charter flight). Check in to a luxury Franz Josef lodge. Afternoon walk through the glacier valley to orient yourself.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at Franz Josef's finest restaurant — enjoy West Coast whitebait fritters (a regional specialty), venison, and local craft beers or wines in a cozy alpine setting.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent in-room breakfast — eggs your way, smoked salmon, pastries, fresh juice, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch en route at a scenic Haast Pass viewpoint — pre-packed premium hamper, or stop at a top-rated café in Wanaka
meals.dinner: Franz Josef fine-dining restaurant — West Coast whitebait fritters, venison loin, and Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: The scenic charter flight from Queenstown to Franz Josef is highly recommended for breathtaking aerial views of the Southern Alps and glaciers. If driving, the Haast Pass route is one of New Zealand's most scenic drives — allow extra time for stops. Book Franz Josef accommodation well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk — self-guided or with a private guide. Explore the terminal face of the famous Franz Josef Glacier on the valley floor walk through ancient rainforest and glacial moraine. Interpretive signage explains the glacier's dramatic retreat. Walk as far as the safety barriers allow for close-up glacier views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Heli-hike on Franz Josef Glacier — the ultimate glacier experience. A helicopter lands you on the upper glacier ice field where a certified guide leads a 3–4 hour ice walk through seracs, crevasses, and ice caves. Crampons and equipment provided. Return by helicopter with aerial views of the glacier and Westland Tai Poutini National Park.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the lodge — hot tub under the stars, followed by a private dinner at the lodge featuring West Coast seafood and premium New Zealand wines.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at the lodge — pancakes with manuka honey, eggs, and fresh West Coast produce
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the glacier — energy bars, sandwiches, and a thermos of hot soup provided by the heli-hike operator
meals.dinner: Private lodge dinner — West Coast crayfish, green-lipped mussels, and a curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: The heli-hike is weather and glacier condition dependent — have a flexible backup plan. Book with Franz Josef Glacier Guides well in advance. The valley walk is free and accessible year-round. November is an excellent time with longer daylight hours. Wear waterproof layers and sturdy footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer or scenic flight to Aoraki Mount Cook National Park (approximately 4–5 hours drive via the West Coast and Mackenzie Basin, or 45-minute scenic charter flight). Arrive at Mount Cook Village and check in to The Hermitage Hotel — the iconic luxury lodge at the base of Aoraki.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Lake — one of New Zealand's most rewarding alpine hikes. Walk through Aoraki Mount Cook National Park past swing bridges, glacial lakes with floating icebergs, and directly toward the towering face of Aoraki (3,724m). Reach Hooker Lake for breathtaking close-up views of the mountain and glacier terminus.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at The Hermitage's fine-dining restaurant — The Alpine Restaurant — with panoramic floor-to-ceiling views of Aoraki Mount Cook illuminated in alpenglow. Enjoy Canterbury lamb and Central Otago wines.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Franz Josef lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the Hooker Valley Track — gourmet hamper with sandwiches, fruit, and sparkling water at Hooker Lake
meals.dinner: The Alpine Restaurant at The Hermitage — Canterbury lamb rack, seasonal vegetables, and Central Otago Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is 10km return and takes approximately 3 hours — suitable for most fitness levels. The track has three swing bridges and ends at Hooker Lake with iceberg views. November offers excellent conditions with wildflowers in bloom. The Hermitage is the only luxury accommodation in Mount Cook Village — book well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Aoraki Mount Cook scenic flight — a 45-minute private fixed-wing or helicopter flight circling the summit of Aoraki, landing on the Tasman Glacier snowfield for a champagne toast at altitude. Unparalleled views of the Southern Alps, Tasman Glacier, and the Mackenzie Basin.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tasman Glacier Boat Tour — board a zodiac inflatable on the Tasman Glacier Lake, weaving through massive icebergs calved from the glacier. A guide explains the glacier's history and the impact of climate change. Return to The Hermitage for afternoon tea.
day_by_day.evening: Final Mount Cook evening — private stargazing experience with a certified Dark Sky guide in the Aoraki Mackenzie International Dark Sky Reserve (one of the world's largest). Observe the Milky Way, Southern Cross, and Magellanic Clouds through high-powered telescopes. Return for a nightcap of aged whisky by the lodge fireplace.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at The Hermitage before the sunrise flight — yogurt, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Afternoon tea at The Hermitage after the glacier boat tour — finger sandwiches, scones with clotted cream, and loose-leaf tea
meals.dinner: The Hermitage fine-dining — blue cod, truffle butter, seasonal greens, and a farewell wine selection

day_by_day.notes: The scenic flight is weather dependent — have a flexible schedule. Book all Mount Cook activities through The Hermitage concierge or directly with Air Safaris and Mount Cook Glacier Tours. The Dark Sky experience is only available on clear nights — November typically offers excellent conditions. Dress very warmly for stargazing.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aoraki Mount Cook — leisurely breakfast with views of the mountain. Optional short walk to Kea Point for a last look at the Mueller Glacier and Aoraki before departure. Pack and check out of The Hermitage.
